body:
## Background

Child of the #7079 stranded-work audit. The laptop's `~/git/fleet` is not a working clone — it is a lane scratch yard wearing a repo's name: a shell clone with 4 tracked files and no remotes, holding 1,581 top-level untracked entries, ~610,000 files, ~242 GB. Composition (measured 2026-11-07): 1,276 `probe-*` throwaway sandboxes, ~240 task dirs, 198 nested clones of the real repos, watcher-bench fixture floods (371k generated `.txt` files), and large duplicated Rust build output (~75k `target/` segments; the 25 largest files are 0.7–1 GB debug binaries duplicated across ID task checkouts). Spot-checked nested clones are clean with heads equal to their live remote tips — nothing is stranded in them. The yard is in LIVE use (new dirs created during the audit itself).

Drew's disposition rule (2026-11-07 21:31 CST): **KEEP text, scripts, and markdown.** The yard's human-authored ephemera is preserved; everything else is reappable.

## Spec — build a scratch-yard reaper for ~/git/fleet

A scheduled, janitor-pattern reaper (same operating rules as the disk janitor), run on the laptop against `~/git/fleet` only.

### KEEP — archive-first
- Every human-authored text/script/markdown file anywhere in the yard: `.md .txt .sh .py .ts .js .json .yaml .yml .toml .log` and equivalent human-authored text (lane logs, PR-body drafts, triage notes, probe scripts, docs).
- The ~92 loose root files are the known-precious set — archive ALL of them.
- Archive exactly like the disk janitor: gather into the dated archive layout (archive branch / janitor archive tree), commit ALL, push, and VERIFY the push landed before any removal of a kept file's original. Nothing kept is ever deleted before its archive copy is verified.

### REAP — only after the keep-archive verifies
- Build output and duplicated bulk: `target/` trees, `.o`/`.d`/`.rmeta`/`.rlib` artifacts, `dist/`, `node_modules/`.
- Bench fixture floods: watcher-bench `.txt` fixtures are GENERATED bulk despite the `.txt` extension — the keep rule covers human-authored text, not fixture floods. The reaper MUST use provenance/size heuristics (fixture dirs by name, per-file and per-dir caps, generated-content markers) to separate fixture bulk from authored text, and its run plan must state the heuristics it applied.
- Nested clones whose heads are verified clean AND equal to their remote tips (nothing unlanded). A nested clone with ANY unlanded state (dirty files, unpushed commits, detached work not on a remote) is archive-first, never reaped blind.

### Safety gates
- Age gate: reap only entries idle ≥ 4 hours (the janitor's rule). The yard is in live use — never touch an entry with recent mtimes, an attached live process, or a registered worktree pointing into it.
- No recursive/wildcard deletes of anything not inventoried by the run's own scan; every reap is a named entry from the run report.
- First runs are dry-run/report-only until the keep-archive path is proven end-to-end.

### Report per run
- GB reclaimed, files kept/archived (count + archive ref), entries reaped (count + GB), entries skipped (active or dirty) BY NAME.

## Acceptance
- Reaper exists as a repeatable tool + schedule on the laptop, scoped to `~/git/fleet`.
- One full run report demonstrating: keep-archive verified before reap, age gate respected, live entries untouched, GB reclaimed counted.
- The ~242 GB yard trends down without losing a single human-authored file.

## Acceptance criteria

- The reaper exists as a repeatable tool plus a schedule on the laptop, scoped to `~/git/fleet` only.
- The keep-archive (all human-authored text/scripts/markdown, including the ~92 loose root files) is committed, pushed, and the push verified BEFORE any kept file's original is removed.
- Reaping respects the safety gates: entries idle ≥ 4 hours only, no live-process or registered-worktree entries touched, no recursive/wildcard deletes — every reap is a named entry from the run's own scan.
- Bench fixture floods are separated from authored text by stated provenance/size heuristics recorded in the run report.
- One full run report demonstrates: keep-archive verified before reap, age gate respected, live entries untouched, GB reclaimed counted, entries kept/reaped/skipped (by name) listed.
- The ~242 GB yard trends down without losing a single human-authored file.
